## Exact assumptions and conditional bounds

- [`sat26-sparse`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-sparse)
- [`sat26-reported-formal`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-reported-formal)

Conditional on `sat26-sparse`:

$$
2^{O(m/\sqrt{\log m})}L^{O(1)}
$$

Alternatively, conditional on `sat26-reported-formal`:

$$
2^{O(m(\log\log m)^2/\sqrt{\log m})}L^{O(1)}
$$

The resulting algorithm is deterministic and uses polynomial space, conditional on the corresponding assumption and this derivation. $L$ denotes the original input length; constants may depend on the stated fixed constants. Logarithms in asymptotic bounds may be regularized when the declared measure is small.

## Preprocessing

Remove isolated vertices, which do not affect edge domination. Handle m = 0 directly; otherwise the remaining graph has at most 2m vertices. For threshold queries, handle budgets outside [0,m] directly.

## Encoding size

| Quantity | Bound |
| --- | --- |
| Boolean variables, including auxiliaries | $O(m)$ |
| Clauses | $O(m)$ |
| Maximum clause width | $3$ |

## Derivation

1. For each edge e introduce a selection bit x_e. For each nonisolated vertex v, introduce an endpoint indicator z_v and enforce that z_v is true exactly when at least one selected edge is incident with v.

2. Implement $z_v\leftrightarrow\bigvee_{e\ni v}x_e$ with binary OR gates and full equivalences. Degree-one vertices need only an equality with their incident edge bit. There are $O(\sum_v\deg(v))=O(m)$ gates in total; each gate has a constant number of clauses of width at most three.

3. For every edge uv add $z_u\vee z_v$. This holds exactly when uv is selected or shares an endpoint with a selected edge. Add the cardinality encoding $\sum_e x_e\le b$ for a queried budget b, using [METHODS.md, Section 2](../../METHODS.md).

4. The threshold formula has N = O(m), M = O(m), and width at most three. Every selected edge set has a unique gate extension. Thus the fixed-density SAT assumption, with forced-zero padding if needed, decides the threshold in B(m) times a polynomial in the original input length L. All construction and gate evaluation costs are polynomial.

5. Binary search over b in [0,m] finds the optimum with O(log(m+1)) threshold queries. Keep the optimum budget, then fix each edge bit to zero if the resulting formula is satisfiable, and to one otherwise. At most m further SAT queries recover an optimum set; added unit clauses preserve the size and width bounds. Calls are sequential, so the stated time and polynomial-space bound hold.

## Caveats and comparison limits

- The exponent is measured in edges m. It yields B(n) on classes with m = O(n), but does not establish a vertex-based subexponential bound for arbitrary dense graphs.
- This entry does not assert an A(k) or B(k) bound for the solution budget k on general graphs. See the general-k candidate and the separate fixed-maximum-degree FPT entry.
- The edge-selection variables number m before auxiliary variables are added. A direct line-graph construction or separate long domination clauses is not needed; shared endpoint OR circuits keep the total at O(m).
- No weighted objective or latest-best comparison is claimed.

The derivation must preserve the objective and account for the encoding length of numerical values; a decision consequence alone does not establish the stated optimization bound.
